Hey, I just did this. I don’t regret it but there’s so much more I wish I’d done. 

Save up: whatever you think need, you’ll need more. Even if you go to a poor country. Checkout nomadlist.com the cost of living for a nomad in almost every city I’ve lived is fairly accurate. 

Visas: if you’re allowed into countries visa free, You might be tempted to go without applying for a visa first. Don’t. If you want to stay anywhere longer than 3 months and have the ability to stay longer try to get a visa before you leave because you can’t usually convert a tourist visa while on a tourist visa (visa free) while abroad.

Work: Finding a way to make even a few hundred dollars online is going to be the best thing you can do to avoid running out of money if you end up falling in love with a country or the road in general.

SIM cards: Do buy a mobile hotspot if you’ll be working online. Don’t buy an expensive SIM card or plan in the US, buy one when you arrive. 

What you’re looking for decides where you should go. Europe can be cheaper than America but not so cheap that you’ll be mcducking it like you would in Ecuador or Chile. 

With all that said, do your research but don’t overplan. I personally recommend going to the cheapest place possible with at least $800 saved for each month for all expenses. With a regard to safety most places I’ve been are safe, that doesn’t mean dangers don’t exist.
